Negative edge sampling

Source: R/graph-sampling.R
negative_sampling.Rd

Draws node pairs that are not edges. Pairs are drawn uniformly from all allowed pairs by rejection: candidate pairs are sampled uniformly, and pairs that appear in exclude, self loops (unless allowed) and repeats are discarded. For undirected graphs (u, v) and (v, u) are the same pair, each returned pair has u < v, and a pair is excluded if either orientation is in exclude.

Usage

negative_sampling(
  exclude,
  num_nodes = NULL,
  num_samples,
  directed = TRUE,
  allow_self_loops = FALSE,
  num_src = NULL,
  num_dst = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  max_tries = 100L
)

Arguments

exclude

2 by E matrix of known positive pairs to avoid (all known positives, including validation and test edges, for the usual filtered protocol).

num_nodes

Number of nodes (homogeneous graphs).

num_samples

Number of negative pairs.

directed

Treat pairs as ordered.

allow_self_loops

Allow (u, u) pairs.

num_src, num_dst

Node counts for bipartite sampling.

seed

Optional integer seed (see sample_neighbors()).

max_tries

Rejection rounds before giving up.

Value

A 2 by num_samples integer matrix.

Details

For bipartite or typed relations give num_src and num_dst; pairs are then (source of type A, target of type B) and self loops are not special.

Examples

negative_sampling(rbind(c(1, 2), c(2, 3)), num_nodes = 4, num_samples = 3,
                  seed = 1)
#>      [,1] [,2] [,3]
#> [1,]    4    3    3
#> [2,]    2    2    1
